events.name: Route 25: The Angry Mankey
events.intro: The road is lined with torn sacks and spilled grain. Pale tracks lead into the grass, and from the grass comes a sound you can feel in your teeth: a whole troop of Mankey, screaming. They are not angry at you. They have not eaten properly in a week, and someone has been taking what they stored for the winter. You are only the next stranger on the road, and they have no more patience left.

success.text: You set your feet. The screaming stops all at once, and that is worse.
The trail bends away from the road, toward a thread of smoke. Someone has been very careless about hiding what they took.

events.name: Route 25: The Thieves' Camp
events.intro: A rough camp in a hollow: three trainers, a cookfire, and a stack of the troop's food sacks they have stopped bothering to hide. A kid's drawing is pinned to the tent: a Mankey with a crown. They took this winter's food from something that has never once asked anyone for anything.

success.text: Nobody wins an argument against a returned sack and a raised fist. The camp breaks and runs, and you lift the heaviest sack onto your shoulder. It is lighter than it should be. They had already eaten a good part of it.

choices.label: Leave it, and face the troop

success.text: You turn back. The troop is still waiting, and still hungry.

events.name: Route 25: The First Three
events.intro: The grass breaks open. Three Mankey come at once, shoulder to shoulder, and their eyes are not rage so much as hunger wearing rage like a coat. There will be no breaks between them. The troop has fought this way for a week.

success.text: Three bodies hit you at once. You do not get a breath, and you were not going to be offered one.

events.name: Route 25: The Fourth
events.intro: Three are down and breathing hard. No potion, no rest. The fourth Mankey was watching the whole fight, and it has learned something from watching. It does not scream. It simply comes.

success.text: It is smarter than the first three, and angrier, because it understood what you did to its friends.

events.name: Route 25: The Fifth Stands Still
events.intro: The fifth Mankey does not charge. It walks out from the rocks and plants itself in front of the other four, who have crawled back to its feet, scratched and silent. It spreads its arms. It is not here to win. It is here so that nobody else has to be hit again. It looks at you, and for one breath you understand that you are the thing that frightens it.

success.text: It does not attack first. It waits for you to decide what kind of person you are.

events.name: Route 25: The Quiet After
events.intro: The fifth Mankey lies in the grass, and the other four crowd around it, shaking. Nobody screams now. The whole troop is looking at you and at each other, and it is the kind of quiet in which a person decides who they are.

success.text: You look back at the troop. They watch you go. It might be the first time in a week that something has walked toward the thieves instead of away.
The troop saw you come back with the sack. They do not understand every word, but they understand that.

choices.label: Offer your hand to the fifth Mankey

success.text: It sniffs your hand for a long time. It is deciding whether you are as hungry for a fight as it was.

events.name: Route 25: The Thieves' Camp (After)
events.intro: The camp is exactly where the tracks said. The thieves heard the screaming stop and hoped it meant the troop had gone. They are packing the sacks they have not yet eaten into a cart. They see you, and their faces do the arithmetic.

success.text: It is easier than it should be. They were already half-ashamed. You carry the last sack back by hand, and as you walk the road you hear the troop begin to sing, which is not a word anyone has taught them.
You leave the cart where it stands. The troop will remember that.

events.name: Route 25: What the Troop Gave Back
events.intro: The fifth Mankey rises, and the troop parts around it. It walks to the sack you carried and puts a hand flat on the grain, and then it walks to you. It is not a request. It is the first Mankey that has ever stood between a troop and a stranger and then been fed by the stranger. It will come with you, and the rest of the troop will be waiting in the stands.

success.text: It bumps its forehead against your leg, once, hard. The troop watches you go. Not one of them looks angry any more. Mankey will be looking for them in the crowd.

events.name: Route 25: A Mankey Steps Out
events.intro: The fifth Mankey steps out of the circle. It does not trust you, but it has seen what you are willing to fight for. The other four lower their eyes. The troop is still hungry, and it is not yours to feed today. It will follow you and ask nothing, which is its own way of saying a great deal.

success.text: It walks beside you and never quite looks back. The troop watches until the road bends.

events.name: Saffron Fighting Tournament
events.intro: A banner stretched across the dojo yard: THE SAFFRON FIGHTING TOURNAMENT. Thirty-two fighters, Fighting types only, one Pokémon each. The organizer, a woman with a clipboard and a bruise on her chin, looks at your Mankey the way a coach looks at a student they have not met yet. "Only that one steps in," she says. "Everything the rest of you know has to stay at the rail."

success.text: The sign-up sheet has thirty-two names. Yours goes at the bottom, in your own hand. Only your fighter will step onto the mat. Everyone else on your team goes to the rail to watch, and not one of them is happy about it.

The sign-up sheet has thirty-two names. Yours goes at the bottom, in your own hand. Only your fighter will step onto the mat. Everyone else on your team goes to the rail to watch, and not one of them is happy about it.
You leave it for the next trainer.

events.name: Tournament: The Crowd
events.intro: A bell. The gate opens. A noise comes up out of the stands like a wave breaking, and over the PA, a voice that has been waiting all year to say this: "Ladies and gentlemen, thirty-two fighters, five rounds, one belt!" A commentary desk beside the mat has two seats: a retired champion with a broken nose, and a young announcer who has never once stopped talking.

success.text: Row after row of brown fur. The whole Mankey troop came down from Route 25 and is standing on the benches, stamping their feet. Someone has hung a sack of grain from the rail like a banner. Your Mankey sees them and does not move for a long moment.
You scan the rows for brown fur and find none. No one is there for your Mankey. It stands very straight, and it has stopped looking.

events.name: Tournament: Round of 32
events.intro: Round of 32. A Machop with a twin on the rail: the twin is a coach, bellowing instructions and flinching at every hit. "That one is somebody's whole family," says the young announcer. "Do not take it personally."

success.text: Round of 32: Machop steps up, and the crowd rises with it.

events.name: Tournament: Training Montage 1
events.intro: It goes down fighting, and its twin leaps the rail and carries it out in its arms. The crowd applauds that harder than the knockout. The cafeteria-bench montage: you grab a rice ball in one fist and a clipboard in the other. The announcer calls this the quiet part, and says nothing for a moment. Pick what to train: 4 fights are still ahead.

success.text: Heavy bag, tyre drags, stones. Your fighter hits harder for the rest of the bracket. You and your fighter climb the dojo steps again and again until the sun hits the hill.

Slow drills, a hundred counters, learning how to take a hit. Your fighter takes the rest of the bracket a little more easily. You and your fighter climb the dojo steps again and again until the sun hits the hill.

Ladders, ropes, sidesteps until it stops thinking about its feet. Your fighter moves faster for the rest of the bracket. You and your fighter climb the dojo steps again and again until the sun hits the hill.

events.name: Tournament: Round of 16
events.intro: Round of 16. A Hawlucha who spends more time on the ropes than on the mat. It points at people in the crowd, it blows kisses, it waves at the cameras. "It plays to the crowd," says the old champion, "and it is better than it pretends. Watch its feet."

success.text: Round of 16: Hawlucha steps up, and the crowd rises with it.

events.name: Tournament: Training Montage 2
events.intro: It bows to the crowd in defeat, then, quietly, bows to you. The pose was a mask for something sharper. A rooftop at dusk. Somewhere below, a radio plays a song your fighter hums without knowing the words. A scrap of paper falls from your pocket: the bracket, with your name circled in your own handwriting. Pick what to train: 3 fights are still ahead.

success.text: Heavy bag, tyre drags, stones. Your fighter hits harder for the rest of the bracket. You skip stones on the roof tiles. Your fighter throws punches at the dusk until its knuckles ring.

Ladders, ropes, sidesteps until it stops thinking about its feet. Your fighter moves faster for the rest of the bracket. You skip stones on the roof tiles. Your fighter throws punches at the dusk until its knuckles ring.

events.name: Tournament: Quarterfinal
events.intro: Quarterfinal. A Throh in a belt so worn it is the colour of dust. It bows to the crowd, to the referee, to the officials, and to you. "The politest fighter in Saffron," says the announcer. "That is not the same as the gentlest."

success.text: Quarterfinal: Throh steps up, and the crowd rises with it.

events.name: Tournament: Training Montage 3
events.intro: It rises, bows once more, and shakes your fighter's hand with both of its own. You do not remember when you last felt that respected by someone you had just beaten. The sun is rising, and your fighter is already up, shadow-boxing the first light. The Throh from the last round is outside the gate, bowing to the sunrise. It does not say anything. It holds the door. Pick what to train: 2 fights are still ahead.

success.text: Heavy bag, tyre drags, stones. Your fighter hits harder for the rest of the bracket. Someone left a clean towel on the bench. Nobody will admit to it.
Slow drills, a hundred counters, learning how to take a hit. Your fighter takes the rest of the bracket a little more easily. Someone left a clean towel on the bench. Nobody will admit to it.
Ladders, ropes, sidesteps until it stops thinking about its feet. Your fighter moves faster for the rest of the bracket. Someone left a clean towel on the bench. Nobody will admit to it.

events.name: Tournament: Semifinal
events.intro: Semifinal. A Hitmonchan who has not made a sound in four tournaments: no cry, no grunt. Its fists speak. The announcer lowers his voice. "Nobody has ever heard it say a word. The people who have fought it say they did not need to."

success.text: Semifinal: Hitmonchan steps up, and the crowd rises with it.

events.name: Tournament: Training Montage 4
events.intro: It does not cry out when it falls. It lifts its eyes to yours, and for the first time in four years the crowd hears it exhale. That is the loudest thing in the building. The night before the final. The stadium is empty, chairs stacked, floor lights on low. Somewhere a faint cheer from the memory of the afternoon. Your fighter walks out alone, stands in the ring, and stares at the other side. Pick what to train: 1 fight is still ahead.

success.text: Heavy bag, tyre drags, stones. Your fighter hits harder for the rest of the bracket. There is a single rival now, on the other side of a wall, awake too.
Slow drills, a hundred counters, learning how to take a hit. Your fighter takes the rest of the bracket a little more easily. There is a single rival now, on the other side of a wall, awake too.
Ladders, ropes, sidesteps until it stops thinking about its feet. Your fighter moves faster for the rest of the bracket. There is a single rival now, on the other side of a wall, awake too.

events.name: Tournament: The Final
events.intro: The final. Across the mat stands a fighter of your own kind. Its trainer is a tired woman who runs a dojo with a leaking roof. The belt is prize money. If it wins, the dojo stays open and nine children keep their lessons. It looks at your fighter the way you look at your own, and neither of you wants to hurt the other.

success.text: The crowd chants for both of you. In the stands, nobody sits.

win.text: Won the Saffron Fighting Tournament and the belt: the title, Dynamic Punch and Champion's Entrance.

events.name: Tournament: The Final
events.intro: The final. Across the mat stands a fighter of your own kind, and it is crying before the bell. Its trainer is a boy who lost his father, a Black Belt who once fought in this ring. The belt is the only thing he has ever wanted. The announcer finds no joke for it.

success.text: The crowd chants for both of you. In the stands, nobody sits.

win.text: Won the Saffron Fighting Tournament and the belt: the title, Dynamic Punch and Champion's Entrance.

events.name: Tournament: The Final
events.intro: The final. Across the mat stands a fighter of your own kind with a scar through one eyebrow. Its trainer is a stranger from another region who says only: "I came to lose to someone who deserves it. Do not make me wait." The crowd does not know whether to cheer or to hush. Your fighter growls and means it.

success.text: The crowd chants for both of you. In the stands, nobody sits.

win.text: Won the Saffron Fighting Tournament and the belt: the title, Dynamic Punch and Champion's Entrance.

events.name: A Familiar Belt
events.intro: On the path ahead a fighter of your own kind stands very straight, its arms folded across a belt it made itself: red cloth, knotted, bleached with the sun. It does not look at the stands this time. It looks at you, and bows, once, from the waist.

success.text: It is still too proud to say thank you. It grins at you, a flash of teeth. The home-made belt is the best thing it owns. It is nothing like the real one, and it has never looked better.

effects.text: The Tournament rival returned in a home-made belt, and bowed.

success.text: You nod and walk on. It watches you go, belt and all.

events.name: Saffron Fighting Dojo
events.intro: The Fighting Dojo next door is open. Its master, arms folded, offers a one-on-one: his Machamp against your whole team.

success.text: The master bows. Machamp cracks its knuckles.
You bow and leave the dojo.

events.name: Dojo: The Master’s Gift
events.intro: The master nods. "You earned a student. Choose."

success.text: Hitmonlee bows and falls in step beside you.
Hitmonchan bows and falls in step beside you.

events.name: Dojo: The Master’s Gift
events.intro: The master nods, then calls a third student out of the back. "Today I can offer three. Choose."

success.text: Hitmonlee bows and falls in step beside you.
Hitmonchan bows and falls in step beside you.
Hitmontop bows and falls in step beside you.

events.name: The Copycat Girl
events.intro: A girl in a bow follows you down the street, repeating every word you say and every step you take. She holds out a hand: "Copy me! Four claps!"

success.text: You match all four. She squeals, copies your Pokémon’s cry note for note, and hands you a TM: Mimic.

failure.text: You miss a clap. She copies your embarrassed face, giggles, and skips away.

success.text: She copies your wave and your walk, all the way out of town.

events.name: Silph Co.: The Lobby
events.intro: The lobby of the Silph Co. tower: marble floors, a hushed receptionist, a single elevator. The president himself comes down to meet visitors.

success.text: He thanks you for keeping the city safe and hands you a Poké Ball: a Lapras, bred for ferrying people across the water. "Something is wrong upstairs," he adds quietly. The building stays open to you.
Word has gone round that you are being hunted. The guards cross their arms. The lobby is as far as you get.

events.name: Saffron Magnet Train
events.intro: The Magnet Train hums in its station, bound for the coast. A ride would carry you most of the way across, but you would see nothing of the road.

success.text: The city blurs. You step off right beside the Gym, with nothing found along the way.
You watch it glide away without you.

events.name: Sabrina's Labyrinth
events.intro: A fortune-teller in a violet shawl stops you outside the Gym: "Let me read your aura." A town guide hurries over, whispering about a special entrance that few ever see.

success.text: Your Poké Balls rattle, then go quiet. The world tilts.
Your Poké Balls rattle, then go quiet. The world tilts.
You decline. Nothing changes.

events.name: Labyrinth: The First Fight
events.intro: Your Pokémon are scattered across the Labyrinth, locked in shadow lanterns. A hooded shape blocks the corridor. You reach for a Poké Ball and find nothing. The first fight is lost before it begins. A tombstone rises on the dark, a swarm of ghosts flies behind it, and the dark folds into a new scene. A small ghost floats up to you: "I can help you get your body and your Pokémon back."

success.text: Free every lantern, reach Sabrina, and your body comes home.

events.name: Labyrinth: The Possessed Trainer
events.intro: Lantern 1 of 6: one of your Pokémon is trapped inside. A trainer with empty eyes guards it.

success.text: The ghost fights alone.

events.name: Labyrinth: The Mirror Puzzle
events.intro: Lantern 2 of 6: one of your Pokémon is trapped inside. Mirrors line the walls; the real path is the one that reflects true.

success.text: The mirrors part. The lantern opens. A campfire burns warm in the next chamber.

failure.text: The glass shows you a false road and bites back.

events.name: Labyrinth: The Memory Game
events.intro: Lantern 3 of 6: one of your Pokémon is trapped inside. Lights flash in a pattern. Echo it back.

success.text: The lights fall in line. The lantern opens.

failure.text: You lose the thread and the dark pushes back.

events.name: Labyrinth: Two Doors
events.intro: Lantern 4 of 6: one of your Pokémon is trapped inside. Two doors, one lantern. One door is true.

success.text: The true door. The lantern opens, and a campfire waits beyond.

failure.text: A false door. You stumble back out.

success.text: The true door. The lantern opens, and a campfire waits beyond.

failure.text: A false door. You stumble back out.

events.name: Labyrinth: The Balance
events.intro: Lantern 5 of 6: one of your Pokémon is trapped inside. A scale hangs over the lantern. Hold steady until it levels.

success.text: The scale settles. The lantern opens.

failure.text: The scale tips and the weights fall.

events.name: Labyrinth: The Riddle
events.intro: Lantern 6 of 6: one of your Pokémon is trapped inside. A voice from the lantern: "I walk beside you but leave no steps. Cut me down and I still follow. What am I?"

success.text: Wrong. The voice sighs.
The lantern flares open. Only Sabrina remains.
Wrong. The voice sighs.

events.name: Labyrinth: Sabrina's Alakazam
events.intro: Sabrina waits at the heart of the Labyrinth with her Alakazam. "You are only a ghost," she says. "Go back to sleep."

success.text: The ghost faces her alone.

events.name: The Ghost Returns
events.intro: The screen goes black. Silence. Then a face lunges out of the dark, all teeth and eyes, and holds there. It wavers, and the fright melts into something shy. It asks, very quietly, to join your team.

success.text: It has not forgotten the Labyrinth, or you.
It fades, and the dark lets go of the screen.
